q: How does a gas-based DRI steel plant in Libya work out its CBAM figure?
title: Libyan DRI steel: CBAM figure
short: Count natural gas used in the DRI reformer and furnace, carbon in electrodes and charge carbon in the arc furnace, and fuel for reheating. Use a mass balance where carbon stays in the steel. Gas-based DRI usually gives a lower figure than coal or blast furnace routes, which is worth proving.
audience: DRI and arc furnace steel producers in Libya and North Africa

ul: Natural gas to the DRI module.
Electrodes, coke and lime in the arc furnace.
Gas or oil for reheating before rolling.

p: Electricity for the arc furnace is reported but not charged for steel.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, power and production records into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions your EU importer asks for.
